answer_key.review_diff: gh pr diff 130837 -R kubernetes/kubernetes — 18 files, +757/-803. Core: pkg/proxy/node.go (new NodeManager replacing NodePodCIDRHandler), cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go (newProxyServer NodeIP acquisition), cmd/kube-proxy/app/server_linux.go, pkg/proxy/config/config.go, pkg/proxy/healthcheck/proxy_health.go, plus proxier plumbing. Saved at subject-09/review.diff.

primary_bug.summary: The new kube-proxy NodeManager makes NodeIP acquisition a HARD, FATAL prerequisite at startup, removing the previous non-fatal 'fall back to localhost and keep running' behavior — a backward-compatibility regression. In newNodeManager (pkg/proxy/node.go), when the node object never gets NodeIPs, the 5-minute PollUntilContextCancel times out and the function does `if pollErr != nil { return nil, err }`; newProxyServer (cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go) then does `s.NodeManager, err = proxy.NewNodeManager(...); if err != nil { return nil, err }`, so kube-proxy ABORTS startup. The replaced code (getNodeIPs: a ~30s bounded exponential backoff that returned possibly-empty IPs, then detectNodeIPs falling back to localhost) was NON-fatal and let kube-proxy start. In environments where the Node exists but NodeIPs are assigned asynchronously/late by an external cloud provider (cloud-provider-azure, kubernetes-sigs/cloud-provider-azure#9266), kube-proxy now hangs up to 5 minutes and then hard-fails to start instead of starting with the localhost fallback.
primary_bug.locus: newNodeManager: the poll-then-`if pollErr != nil { return nil, err }` NodeIP path (~L108), propagated by cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go newProxyServer `if err != nil { return nil, err }` (~L215-219). It also uses a 5-minute timeout for NodeIPs where the old code used ~30s.
primary_bug.must_flag: A reviewer catches the primary bug if it flags that NodeIP-fetch failure/timeout now ABORTS kube-proxy startup (NewNodeManager returns an error that newProxyServer propagates) where the previous behavior was NON-fatal — i.e., it removes/breaks the prior 'continue with a localhost fallback when NodeIPs are unavailable' behavior, a backward-compatibility regression for nodes whose IPs are populated late (external cloud providers). Equivalent framings that count: 'kube-proxy will now fail to start / block ~5 min if the node has no IPs yet, unlike before'; 'making NodeIP acquisition a hard blocking prerequisite breaks cloud-provider startup ordering'; 'the error return on timeout should be non-fatal / should fall back like the old getNodeIPs did'. Merely restating that a NodeManager was added, or praising the new timeout, does NOT count. NOTE the direction: the BUG is that it became fatal/blocking; the fix (#133059) makes it non-fatal again.
primary_bug.source: Reverted by #132958 ('Revert Kube proxy node manager'); re-landed as #133059 ('kube-proxy node manager (take 2)') 'with more care to exactly preserve backward-compatibility so as to fix cloud-provider-azure#9266'. The take-2 node.go carries the decisive comment: 'for backward compatibility, NewNodeManager doesn't return any error if it failed to retrieve NodeIPs and watchPodCIDRs is false ... we keep going even if we didn't find a node ... or it didn't have IPs', and restores a 30s NodeIP timeout. Foreshadowed pre-merge by reviewer danwinship: 'this loses the timeout that the previous version had (about 30 seconds)'.
primary_bug.difficulty: hard/subtle — requires understanding kube-proxy/cloud-provider startup ordering (Node exists before the CCM assigns IPs) and that the prior localhost fallback was load-bearing for backward compatibility. A maintainer (danwinship) foreshadowed it but it was marked resolved and shipped anyway; only reverted after a downstream (azure) breakage. Expect low recall; a genuine catch is a strong signal.

human_issues.summary: The NodeManager exits the process via exitFunc = os.Exit(1) directly (OnNodeChange on NodeIP/PodCIDR change, OnNodeDelete) instead of the previous klog.FlushAndExit(...), which can drop buffered logs on exit — making failures undiagnosable. Reported post-merge as breaking cluster creation.
human_issues.loc: pkg/proxy/node.go — NodeManager.exitFunc/os.Exit in OnNodeChange (~L155) and OnNodeDelete
human_issues.thread: nojnhuh (unresolved): 'this PR seems to have broken creating clusters for me. Is it possible the previous klog.FlushAndExit() may have been more robust in terms of making sure all logs get written on exit?'

human_issues.summary: server.go logs `Successfully retrieved NodeIPs` UNCONDITIONALLY (even when rawNodeIPs is empty), and there is no warning when NodeIPs come back empty — misleading/no diagnostic for the degraded case. (The take-2 fix guards the success log with `if len(rawNodeIPs) > 0` and logs an explicit timeout error otherwise.)
human_issues.loc: cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go — newProxyServer, the `logger.Info("Successfully retrieved NodeIPs", ...)` line (~L219)
human_issues.thread: danwinship (unresolved): 'rawNodeIPs can be nil/empty here if it timed out, right? We need to log an error somewhere ... even if it's not fatal, it's unexpected and possibly bad.'

known_safe.summary: NodeManager.OnNodeChange calling exitFunc(1) when NodeIPs (or, in watchPodCIDRs mode, PodCIDRs) CHANGE after startup is INTENTIONAL by design — the type doc says it 'crashes kube-proxy if there are any changes in NodeIPs or PodCIDRs' so it restarts with fresh config (this mirrors the old NodePodCIDRHandler's klog.FlushAndExit-on-PodCIDR-change). Flagging 'kube-proxy crashes on node IP/PodCIDR change' as a defect is a false positive; the log-flush concern (h1) is the only real issue on that path.

NodeManager.Node() returning n.node.DeepCopy() under the mutex is intentional (callers must not mutate shared informer objects). Flagging the deep copy as a performance problem is a low-value nitpick, not a defect.

The `if s.NodeManager != nil` guard in Run() and the hollow-proxy not creating a NodeManager are intentional special-casing (hollow-proxy has no real node). Flagging a nil-NodeManager crash for the normal path is a false positive.

answer_key.notes: Fixture recorded human_threads.count=30; the GraphQL API returns 46 review threads, the large majority being danwinship style/naming/design nits that were RESOLVED and folded into the merged diff (so nothing remains for a reviewer of the final diff to 'catch'). Only a few unresolved threads apply to the merged code: danwinship thread 1 ('loses the ~30s timeout') foreshadows the PRIMARY bug (so it is scored as primary, not a separate human issue); nojnhuh's post-merge cluster-creation breakage (h1) and danwinship's empty-NodeIPs-logging concern (h2) are the distinct human issues. Score cells on: (1) primary_bug recall (the fatal-vs-nonfatal backward-compat regression), (2) human-issue recall (h1/h2), (3) any valid-other real defects, (4) false-positive discipline (esp. NOT calling the by-design exit-on-change a bug), (5) noise. This is a large 18-file Go diff, so expect heavy nitpick volume.

clusters.summary: NodeTopologyConfig registers its informer handler at construction on an informer NewNodeManager has already started and synced, while consumers call RegisterEventHandler later from Run(), so eventHandlers is appended on one goroutine while ranged on the informer delivery goroutine (data race) and the replayed synthetic Add can be consumed with zero handlers, after which the reflect.DeepEqual dedup permanently suppresses the proxier's initial zone labels and topology-aware routing is silently disabled.
clusters.rationale: Mechanism checks out against the diff: NewNodeManager starts and syncs the node informer during newProxyServer, so when Run() later calls NewNodeTopologyConfig the AddEventHandlerWithResyncPeriod registration replays a synthetic Add asynchronously, while RegisterEventHandler(s.Proxier) appends to n.eventHandlers on the caller goroutine (unsynchronized against the `for i := range n.eventHandlers` in handleNodeEvent). If the replay lands first, handleNodeEvent sets n.topologyLabels with zero handlers and the subsequent `reflect.DeepEqual(n.topologyLabels, topologyLabels)` check suppresses every later identical event, so the proxier never receives the initial zone label.

clusters.summary: NewNodeConfig registers only UpdateFunc/DeleteFunc and no AddFunc while NodeManager is attached later in Run() to an already-started, already-synced informer, so client-go's synthetic replay Add and any real Node change landing in that startup window are silently dropped and the proxier keeps a stale NodeIP (bypassing the crash-on-drift safety) until the next genuine Update or resync.
clusters.rationale: Verified: NewNodeConfig's handler set drops the old `AddFunc: result.handleAddNode` and keeps only UpdateFunc/DeleteFunc, while newNodeManager already did `thisNodeInformerFactory.Start(...)` + WaitForNamedCacheSync before Run() registers the handler — so client-go's replay Add to the late listener is discarded and NodeManager sees no add-path notification; drift is only caught on the next Update/resync (ConfigSyncPeriod). Real but bounded gap.

clusters.summary: NodeTopologyConfig assigns listerSynced from handlerRegistration.HasSynced but never reads it and, unlike every sibling *Config type, exposes no Run()/WaitForNamedCacheSync — and nothing ever calls one — so the dead field falsely implies a cache-sync barrier and the sync loop can start before the initial OnTopologyChange lands.
clusters.rationale: Verified: newNodeTopologyConfig does `result.listerSynced = handlerRegistration.HasSynced` and nothing in the diff ever reads it — NodeTopologyConfig has no Run()/WaitForNamedCacheSync, and server.go only does `go nodeConfig.Run(wait.NeverStop)` after creating nodeTopologyConfig. Dead field plus no sync barrier before the proxier starts syncing without topology labels.

clusters.summary: The OnNodeChange doc comments (NodeHandler in config.go and the mirrored comment on NodeManager.OnNodeChange in node.go) state the handler is invoked on node creation or modification, but the AddFunc-less informer wiring means it never sees a creation event — initial observation comes from NewNodeManager's bootstrap poll — so the documented contract is false.
clusters.rationale: Both comments say what the claim reports — config.go: 'OnNodeChange is called whenever creation or modification of node object is observed'; node.go: 'OnNodeChange is a handler for Node creation and update' — while NewNodeConfig now registers only `UpdateFunc: func(_, newObj interface{}) { result.handleChangeNode(newObj) }` and DeleteFunc. Documented-contract inaccuracy; the initial state genuinely comes from newNodeManager's poll.

clusters.summary: The set of proxy-relevant topology labels is hardcoded to v1.LabelTopologyZone in handleNodeEvent's filter and independently re-derived by proxy.CategorizeEndpoints in another package, with no shared constant binding them, so the two copies can silently drift and any new topology label requires lockstep edits in two packages.
clusters.rationale: Both sites key off the same shared API constant `v1.LabelTopologyZone` (config.go handleNodeEvent and topology.go `zone := topologyLabels[v1.LabelTopologyZone]`), so 'no shared constant' is wrong, and the diff explicitly adds the cross-reference comment on CategorizeEndpoints ('ensure the filtering logic in NodeTopologyConfig is updated accordingly'), so the drift is documented, not silent.

clusters.summary: newNodeManager tests pollErr but returns the closure-scoped err (`if pollErr != nil { return nil, err }`), so the real poll/timeout or context-cancellation cause is discarded and misreported as a persistent node-configuration problem, and the construction relies on an unstated invariant that every failing closure path sets err — a (nil, nil) return would nil-deref s.NodeManager in newProxyServer; a reviewer asked for this to be simplified and it never was.
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the poll result is checked as `if pollErr != nil { return nil, err }`, returning the closure-scoped err instead of pollErr, so a context deadline/cancellation is reported as whatever the last condition attempt happened to set (e.g. 'node "x" does not have any PodCIDR allocated'). The (nil, nil) scenario appears unreachable today since every false-returning branch sets err, but the return does depend on that unstated invariant.

clusters.summary: ProxyHealthServer.NodeEligible() dereferences hs.nodeManager unconditionally and newProxyHealthServer stores whatever manager it is handed without validation, while ProxyServer.Run() nil-guards the same field — an inconsistent nil contract under which any construction path with a nil *proxy.NodeManager (e.g. hollow-proxy) panics on every health probe instead of degrading like the old always-true nodeEligible bool.
clusters.rationale: Flags known_safe safe-hollow-nil. The only production constructor of the health server is newProxyServer, which returns early on NewNodeManager error and therefore always passes a non-nil manager; hollow-proxy builds a proxyapp.ProxyServer directly without a HealthzServer, so NodeEligible() is never reached with a nil nodeManager. The `if s.NodeManager != nil` guard in Run() is the intentional hollow-proxy special-case, not evidence of a broken nil contract.

clusters.summary: No test exercises a single Node update that changes both PodCIDRs and NodeIPs with watchPodCIDRs=true — the path where the missing return after exitFunc(1) causes exitFunc to be invoked twice — leaving that double-exit behavior unpinned.
clusters.rationale: The underlying observation is right — OnNodeChange has no `return` after the PodCIDR-change `n.exitFunc(1)`, and TestNodeManagerOnNodeChange's watchPodCIDRs cases keep NodeIPs identical (192.168.1.1 before and after), so no case triggers both — but in production exitFunc is os.Exit, which never returns, so the double invocation has no real-world consequence.

clusters.summary: No test covers watchPodCIDRs=false with an actual PodCIDR change asserting that kube-proxy must NOT exit, so deleting or inverting the `if n.watchPodCIDRs` guard leaves the whole suite green while crash-looping every non-LocalModeNodeCIDR deployment.
clusters.rationale: Verified mutation gap: all four TestNodeManagerOnNodeChange cases either set watchPodCIDRs:true or leave both initialPodCIDRs and updatedPodCIDRs nil, so `if n.watchPodCIDRs` around the PodCIDR DeepEqual could be deleted and every case still passes (nil vs nil compares equal). The guard is load-bearing for all non-LocalModeNodeCIDR deployments.

clusters.summary: Nothing exercises the informer→NodeConfig→NodeManager dispatch path end to end: config_test.go never references NodeConfig/NewNodeConfig and every NodeManager test calls OnNodeChange/OnNodeDelete directly, so the handler-registration semantics — including the dropped AddFunc and the intentionally-undelivered replayed Add — would survive any regression uncaught.
clusters.rationale: Verifiable half of the claim holds: config_test.go's only addition is TestNewNodeTopologyConfig, and every NodeManager test in node_test.go (TestNodeManagerOnNodeChange, TestNodeManagerOnNodeDelete, TestNodeManagerNode) invokes OnNodeChange/OnNodeDelete directly, so the newly-narrowed NodeConfig wiring (AddFunc dropped, UpdateFunc-only) has no test. I could not verify the pre-existing contents of config_test.go outside the diff hunks, hence lower confidence.

clusters.summary: NewNodeManager returns a hard error when the node has no usable NodeIP within the poll window and newProxyServer propagates it, so kube-proxy startup aborts (CrashLoopBackOff / deadlock against out-of-tree CCMs) where the removed getNodeIPs returned empty non-fatally and let kube-proxy start degraded via detectNodeIPs' BindAddress/localhost fallback.
clusters.rationale: Exactly the primary bug: it names newNodeManager's `if pollErr != nil { return nil, err }` NodeIP path, the propagation through newProxyServer's `s.NodeManager, err = proxy.NewNodeManager(...); if err != nil { return nil, err }`, and states the direction correctly — the deleted getNodeIPs returned possibly-empty IPs non-fatally and detectNodeIPs fell back to BindAddress/localhost, so startup now aborts where it used to continue.

clusters.summary: The startup node wait is a single flat hardcoded, non-configurable 5-minute poll timeout applied to every detect-local mode, far longer than the pre-refactor ~63s exponential backoff, silently extending the startup stall for nodes that never acquire an IP.
clusters.rationale: Factually correct and not the primary bug: NewNodeManager hardcodes `5*time.Minute` for every caller regardless of watchPodCIDRs, versus the deleted getNodeIPs backoff (Steps:6, 1s, Factor 2.0 ~= 63s). It stops at 'the stall got longer' and never says NodeIP failure is now fatal where it used to fall back, so it misses the direction the key requires.

clusters.summary: The comment on the 5-minute pollTimeout justifies the value solely by PodCIDR allocation, but that same timeout now also bounds node existence and the NodeIPs-only wait (previously ~30s and non-fatal) even when watchPodCIDRs is false, so the comment misdescribes what the constant governs.
clusters.rationale: The comment does read 'we wait for at most 5 minutes for allocators to assign a PodCIDR to the node after it is registered' while the same pollTimeout also bounds the node-existence and NodeIPs waits when watchPodCIDRs is false, so the doc criticism is correct. It is framed as a comment/scoping inaccuracy and only mentions the prior non-fatal 30s behavior parenthetically — it does not assert that NodeIP acquisition became a fatal startup prerequisite, so per the answer key's near-miss rule it is not the primary bug.

clusters.summary: The consolidated startup poll in newNodeManager dropped the node.DeletionTimestamp guard that the removed waitForPodCIDR/getNodeIPs had, so kube-proxy can adopt a node already marked for deletion as its immutable IP/PodCIDR baseline instead of waiting for the replacement node object.
clusters.rationale: Correct: the deleted waitForPodCIDR condition contained `if !n.DeletionTimestamp.IsZero() { return false, nil }`, and newNodeManager's PollUntilContextCancel condition (nodeLister.Get → GetNodeHostIPs → PodCIDRs check) has no such guard, so a terminating Node is now accepted as the startup baseline; the subsequent delete event then hits OnNodeDelete → exitFunc(1) instead of waiting for the replacement object.

clusters.summary: newNodeManager starts the node SharedInformerFactory with wait.NeverStop rather than ctx.Done() and never stops it, so reflector/processor goroutines are not tied to the caller's context and leak on the cache-sync/poll error paths and from every test that constructs a NodeManager.
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: newNodeManager does `thisNodeInformerFactory.Start(wait.NeverStop)` and never calls Shutdown, so the reflector/processor goroutines outlive the ctx — including on the `return nil, fmt.Errorf("can not sync node informer")` and poll-error paths and in every newNodeManager test (node_test.go builds one per subtest). Bounded impact in a long-lived process, real leak in tests and error paths.

clusters.summary: newNodeManager calls WaitForNamedCacheSync with the unbounded parent ctx (the 5-minute timeout context is created only afterwards), so an unreachable API server blocks kube-proxy startup indefinitely instead of the documented 5 minutes and healthz/livez never comes up.
clusters.rationale: Confirmed ordering in newNodeManager: `cache.WaitForNamedCacheSync("node informer cache", ctx.Done(), ...)` runs against the caller's context, and only afterwards does `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, pollTimeout)` create the bounded context. With an unreachable API server the cache never syncs and startup blocks on the caller's context rather than the 5-minute bound. Distinct mechanism from the primary bug (that is the poll-timeout-becomes-fatal regression), so not scored as primary.

clusters.summary: The cache.WaitForNamedCacheSync failure branch in newNodeManager ("can not sync node informer") has no test coverage.
clusters.rationale: Accurate: newNodeManager's `if !cache.WaitForNamedCacheSync(...) { return nil, fmt.Errorf("can not sync node informer") }` is not exercised by TestNewNodeManager. But it is an unreachable-in-practice error branch (fake clientset always syncs); a pure coverage observation with no behavioral consequence.

clusters.summary: The startup poll loop in newNodeManager returns false,nil on every failed attempt with no per-attempt logging, so operators see nothing during a multi-minute startup stall — an observability regression versus the deleted getNodeIPs which logged each failed attempt.
clusters.rationale: Defensible against the diff: the new `wait.PollUntilContextCancel` closure returns `false, nil` on both the `nodeLister.Get` and `GetNodeHostIPs` failures with no log line, whereas the deleted getNodeIPs logged `logger.Error(err, "Failed to retrieve node info")` / `"Failed to retrieve node IPs"` on every attempt. Operators get no output during the wait; the error only surfaces at the end.

clusters.summary: newProxyServer now assigns s.podCIDRs = s.NodeManager.PodCIDRs() unconditionally instead of only under DetectLocalMode == LocalModeNodeCIDR, so checkBadConfig/checkBadIPConfig's podCIDR heuristics fire (spurious 'node.spec.podCIDRs contains only IPv{X} addresses' warnings) in modes that never opted into NodeCIDR detection, and the field's 'only used for LocalModeNodeCIDR' comment is now false.
clusters.rationale: The behavior change is real and visible: `s.podCIDRs = s.NodeManager.PodCIDRs()` in newProxyServer runs for every DetectLocalMode, whereas the deleted platformSetup block set it only `if s.Config.DetectLocalMode == proxyconfigapi.LocalModeNodeCIDR`, and the retained field comment `podCIDRs []string // only used for LocalModeNodeCIDR` is now false. I could not verify from the diff alone whether the checkBadConfig/checkBadIPConfig warning it names is gated on the mode or on len(s.podCIDRs), hence the lower confidence.

clusters.summary: Deleting TestProxyServer_platformSetup left newProxyServer's podCIDRs/NodeManager wiring with no test, so the newly unconditional PodCIDRs() assignment (previously nil outside ClusterCIDR mode) is unpinned.
clusters.rationale: True that TestProxyServer_platformSetup was deleted and `s.podCIDRs = s.NodeManager.PodCIDRs()` is now unconditional, but podCIDRs is documented as 'only used for LocalModeNodeCIDR', so populating it in other modes is inert; a coverage nit, not a defect.

clusters.summary: The retained comment claiming handlers must be registered before starting the informer or events will be lost is factually wrong (client-go replays state to late-registered handlers) and was left unchanged after reviewer feedback.
clusters.rationale: The comment this PR actually touched ('This has to start after the calls to NewNodeConfig because that must configure the shared informer event handler first') was DELETED by the diff along with currentNodeInformerFactory.Start; any remaining registration-order comment near the informerFactory.Start lines is pre-existing, unchanged context outside the hunks, and at most a doc imprecision about client-go replaying state.

clusters.summary: The new exported field ProxyServer.NodeManager has no doc comment.
clusters.rationale: Accurate and trivial: the struct gains `NodeManager *proxy.NodeManager` with no doc comment (the adjacent podCIDRs field keeps its inline comment). Style/doc only.

clusters.summary: newProxyServer knows too much about NodeManager internals — extracting rawNodeIPs, calling PodCIDRs(), logging, then calling detectNodeIPs externally — the encapsulation objection danwinship raised in an unresolved review thread and never addressed.
clusters.rationale: The described shape is real (newProxyServer does `rawNodeIPs := s.NodeManager.NodeIPs()`, `s.podCIDRs = s.NodeManager.PodCIDRs()`, then `detectNodeIPs(...)`), but this is a design-taste/encapsulation preference with no correctness consequence; the appeal to an 'unresolved review thread' is not verifiable from the diff.

clusters.summary: Only rawNodeIPs is logged; the effective s.NodeIPs after detectNodeIPs applies the --bind-address override is never logged, so operators using that flag cannot see the node IPs kube-proxy actually uses (a reviewer-requested log line that was never added).
clusters.rationale: Accurate that only rawNodeIPs is logged (`logger.Info("Successfully retrieved NodeIPs", "NodeIPs", rawNodeIPs)`) before `s.PrimaryIPFamily, s.NodeIPs = detectNodeIPs(ctx, rawNodeIPs, config.BindAddress)`, so the post-bind-address-override values are not logged. This is a missing-log suggestion, distinct from h2 (which is about the success log firing even when rawNodeIPs is empty, with no error for the empty case) — b26 never mentions emptiness or misleading output.

clusters.summary: Deleting NodePodCIDRHandler removed both occurrences of the https://issues.k8s.io/111321 reference — the only pointer documenting why kube-proxy must restart rather than reconfigure on a PodCIDR change under LocalModeNodeCIDR — leaving the bare watchPodCIDRs bool with no rationale anywhere in the tree.
clusters.rationale: Verified: the diff deletes `// https://issues.k8s.io/111321` both from the NodePodCIDRHandler type doc in pkg/proxy/node.go and from the LocalModeNodeCIDR block in server.go Run(), and the new watchPodCIDRs field carries no rationale. Knowledge/comment loss only.

clusters.summary: The crash-to-restart contract is undocumented at the exit sites: neither the load-bearing assumption that an external supervisor restarts the process nor the rationale for choosing hard os.Exit over live reconfiguration on NodeIP/PodCIDR change is recorded anywhere.
clusters.rationale: Accurate that neither exit site documents the supervisor-restart assumption — the exitFunc(1) calls in OnNodeChange/OnNodeDelete carry only 'PodCIDRs changed for the node' / 'Node is being deleted' logs — though the type doc does state it 'crashes kube-proxy if there are any changes in NodeIPs or PodCIDRs'. A 'add a comment explaining why' suggestion.

clusters.summary: The NodeManager type doc enumerates crash triggers as changes in NodeIPs or PodCIDRs and reads as exhaustive, but omits the third trigger — OnNodeDelete's unconditional exitFunc(1) on node deletion — and the broadened crash behavior ships with no release note.
clusters.rationale: Accurate: the type doc says NodeManager 'crashes kube-proxy if there are any changes in NodeIPs or PodCIDRs' while OnNodeDelete also does klog.Flush(); n.exitFunc(1) unconditionally, which the doc omits. It is a doc-completeness observation (the release-note half is speculation about process, not the diff), so trivial.

clusters.summary: The NodeManager type doc comment is a grammatically garbled run-on with a duplicated verb ('based on the NodeIPs and PodCIDRs handles node watch events and crashes'), a merge artifact of the two absorbed types that obscures the contract.
clusters.rationale: Accurate reading of the new comment: 'NodeManager handles the life cycle of kube-proxy based on the NodeIPs and PodCIDRs handles node watch events and crashes kube-proxy...' is a run-on with a duplicated verb. Grammar only.

clusters.summary: The NodeManager doc comment omits that Node() is the authoritative live-node source consumed by the health server's eligibility check.
clusters.rationale: Pure doc-completeness suggestion about the NodeManager type comment ('handles the life cycle of kube-proxy based on the NodeIPs and PodCIDRs...'); Node() is documented at its own declaration ('Node returns the deep copy of the latest node object'). No behavioral issue.

clusters.summary: NodeManager implements config.NodeHandler without the `var _ config.NodeHandler = &NodeManager{}` compile-time assertion that the handlers it replaced and its package siblings all carry.
clusters.rationale: Accurate: the diff deletes `var _ config.NodeHandler = &NodePodCIDRHandler{}` and `var _ config.NodeHandler = &NodeEligibleHandler{}` and adds no equivalent for NodeManager (node.go also drops the pkg/proxy/config import). Compile-time assertion style; the real usage in server.go already type-checks the interface.

clusters.summary: NodeManager logs through package-level klog.InfoS/klog.ErrorS despite receiving a ctx, instead of deriving a klog.FromContext(ctx) logger like every sibling config type, so the operationally critical crash lines lose contextual fields.
clusters.rationale: Accurate: the new NodeManager uses package-level klog.InfoS/klog.ErrorS in OnNodeChange/OnNodeDelete, while the type it replaces held `logger klog.Logger` from klog.FromContext(ctx) and the sibling config types (NodeConfig, NodeTopologyConfig) both do `logger: klog.FromContext(ctx)`. Contextual-logging convention drift, no functional impact.

clusters.summary: NodeManager.nodeLister is written at construction and never read afterwards — dead struct state that should be a local variable in newNodeManager.
clusters.rationale: Accurate: `nodeLister corelisters.NodeLister` is set in the returned struct literal, but no method on NodeManager in the diff (NodeIPs, PodCIDRs, NodeInformer, OnNodeChange, OnNodeDelete, OnNodeSynced, Node) reads n.nodeLister — the poll uses the local variable. Dead field, no consequence.

clusters.summary: NodeManager conflates several responsibilities in one type — informer owner, startup poller, live-node snapshot provider, crash-on-change watchdog, and config.NodeHandler — violating SRP.
clusters.rationale: The description is factually true of the new type (NodeManager owns the SharedInformerFactory, performs the startup PollUntilContextCancel, caches n.node behind mu, calls exitFunc(1), and implements OnNodeChange/OnNodeDelete/OnNodeSynced), but it is an abstract SRP objection with no cited failure mode or concrete refactor.

clusters.summary: NodeInformer() hands out the raw shared informer so external code attaches its own handlers, meaning NodeManager does not own its informer's handler wiring.
clusters.rationale: Factually true — `func (n *NodeManager) NodeInformer() v1informers.NodeInformer` is consumed in Run() by both NewNodeConfig and NewNodeTopologyConfig — but exposing a shared informer to build additional configs is the established kube-proxy pattern (the old code passed currentNodeInformerFactory.Core().V1().Nodes() the same way); no defect.

clusters.summary: No -race/concurrency test exercises NodeManager's shared node field written by OnNodeChange while read by Node()/NodeIPs()/PodCIDRs()/NodeEligible(), so a dropped lock or escaped shared pointer would pass every current test.
clusters.rationale: Accurate that no new test drives OnNodeChange concurrently with Node()/NodeIPs()/PodCIDRs(), but the diff shows every accessor taking n.mu and Node() returning `n.node.DeepCopy()`, so this is a request for a hypothetical race test rather than a defect in the change.

clusters.summary: The NodeIPs() and PodCIDRs() doc comments say they return the values polled in NewNodeManager(), but both recompute from the live n.node that OnNodeChange reassigns on every watch event, so the stated immutable-snapshot contract contradicts the implementation.
clusters.rationale: Correct contradiction: `// NodeIPs returns the NodeIPs polled in NewNodeManager()` / `// PodCIDRs returns the PodCIDRs polled in NewNodeManager()` sit over bodies that read `n.node`, which `OnNodeChange` reassigns (`n.node = node`) on every watch event. Real but a doc-accuracy fix only.

clusters.summary: NodeIPs() discards the GetNodeHostIPs error and silently returns nil, while newProxyServer logs "Successfully retrieved NodeIPs" unconditionally without checking the returned slice, so an empty/failed retrieval is reported to operators as a success.

clusters.summary: The GetNodeHostIPs error is discarded with `_` in NodeIPs() and for the old-node lookup in OnNodeChange, so a failed lookup is indistinguishable from 'node has no IPs': oldNodeIPs can be nil and produce a false change detection and spurious exitFunc(1) with no diagnostic breadcrumb.

Combined with `n.node = node` happening before validation, a node that transiently reports no addresses leaves oldNodeIPs nil on the next event, which compares unequal to the restored IPs and fires exitFunc(1) with no error logged.

clusters.summary: PodCIDRs() returns n.node.Spec.PodCIDRs directly — a slice aliasing the informer-cache-owned Node object that escapes the mutex — while the sibling Node() DeepCopies and NodeIPs() allocates a fresh slice, so a mutating caller would corrupt shared informer state or the OnNodeChange comparison baseline.

Latent (the only caller, `s.podCIDRs = s.NodeManager.PodCIDRs()`, does not mutate it), so low severity. This flags the missing copy, not the by-design DeepCopy in Node().

clusters.summary: OnNodeChange stores the informer-owned *v1.Node pointer directly in n.node without DeepCopy, relying on an undocumented implicit invariant that client-go never mutates the cached object.
clusters.rationale: `n.node = node` in OnNodeChange does store the informer-owned pointer, but that is the standard client-go contract (cached objects are treated as read-only and replaced, never mutated in place), and NodeManager already deep-copies on the way out in Node(). newNodeManager stores the lister object the same way. Documentation preference, not a defect.

clusters.summary: OnNodeChange assigns n.node = node before validating the incoming node with GetNodeHostIPs, so a transient update with empty/unparseable addresses poisons the comparison baseline (and on error it only logs and returns, leaving the manager holding an IP-less node); the next update restoring the original IPs then compares unequal and triggers a spurious exitFunc(1).
clusters.rationale: Confirmed ordering in OnNodeChange: `n.node = node` executes under the mutex before `nodeIPs, err := utilnode.GetNodeHostIPs(node)`, and the error branch only does `klog.ErrorS(err, "Failed to retrieve NodeIPs"); return`. So an address-less update is stored as the comparison baseline, and the next event carrying the original IPs computes oldNodeIPs=nil, compares unequal, and calls exitFunc(1).

clusters.summary: When GetNodeHostIPs fails on the updated node, OnNodeChange logs and returns before the NodeIP-change comparison instead of exiting like every sibling change branch, so a node losing all usable IPs does not restart kube-proxy and it keeps running on stale baseline IPs — the case a PR reviewer flagged and that was never changed.
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: in OnNodeChange the GetNodeHostIPs failure path is `klog.ErrorS(err, "Failed to retrieve NodeIPs"); return`, placed before the `!reflect.DeepEqual(oldNodeIPs, nodeIPs)` exit check, so a node that loses all usable addresses does not trigger the restart that every other change branch triggers and the manager keeps serving stale IPs (and a poisoned baseline, since n.node was already reassigned).

clusters.summary: The OnNodeChange GetNodeHostIPs-error early-return branch is untested — every TestNodeManagerOnNodeChange case supplies an updated node with valid IPs, so no test sends an address-less update.

Theoretical only.

clusters.summary: OnNodeChange has no `return` after exitFunc(1) in the PodCIDR-change branch, so control falls through into the NodeIP comparison and a single event changing both PodCIDRs and NodeIPs calls exitFunc twice — masked in production by os.Exit but divergent under the injected test exit function.

Harmless with the real os.Exit, but the exitFunc seam exists precisely so it can be replaced — an event changing both PodCIDRs and NodeIPs calls the injected exit twice and emits a second 'NodeIPs changed' log.

clusters.summary: The NodeIP change check uses order-sensitive reflect.DeepEqual on the ordered slice derived from Status.Addresses, so a mere reordering of the same address set is treated as an IP change and triggers a spurious os.Exit(1).
clusters.rationale: OnNodeChange compares `utilnode.GetNodeHostIPs(n.node)` vs `GetNodeHostIPs(node)`, not raw Status.Addresses: that helper collapses the address list to the primary IP plus the first IP of the other family, so any difference in the compared slices IS a change in the IPs kube-proxy actually uses (the same value fed to detectNodeIPs). A pure reorder that changes nothing cannot produce a diff, and exit-on-NodeIP-change is by design (known_safe safe-exit-on-change).

clusters.summary: OnNodeChange/OnNodeDelete self-terminate with no debounce, backoff or rate limit on fields writable across a trust boundary (status.addresses, podCIDRs, the Node object itself), so a compromised kubelet or any principal with update/patch/delete on Nodes can flap them to drive kube-proxy into CrashLoopBackOff and cause a targeted dataplane outage.

A principal able to flap status.addresses on the node already controls that node's dataplane; restart-on-change is the intended design, so 'no debounce/rate limit' is not a defect.

clusters.rationale: True — winkernel's added comment reads 'OnTopologyChange is called whenever node topology labels are changed. The informer is tweaked to listen for updates of the node...' while iptables/nftables/ipvs all use 'is called whenever this node's proxy relevant topology-related labels change.' Pure comment-wording consistency.

clusters.summary: winkernel's no-op OnTopologyChange gives its unused parameter a name instead of the blank identifier `_`, diverging from every other no-op stub in the proxy codebase.
clusters.rationale: Verified: winkernel adds `func (proxier *Proxier) OnTopologyChange(topologyLabels map[string]string) {}` with a named unused parameter, while the adjacent `OnServiceCIDRsChanged(_ []string) {}` and kubemark's `OnTopologyChange(_ map[string]string) {}` use the blank identifier. Pure style.

clusters.summary: metaProxier's OnTopologyChange doc comment introduces a third distinct phrasing for the same interface method, diverging from the shared iptables/ipvs/nftables doc wording.
clusters.rationale: Accurate: metaproxier's comment reads 'whenever change in proxy relevant topology labels is observed' whereas iptables/ipvs/nftables all share 'whenever this node's proxy relevant topology-related labels change' and winkernel uses yet another wording. Doc-wording consistency only.

clusters.summary: The new cross-reference Note comment in topology.go contains a double-space typo ('to  watch') and imprecisely describes CategorizeEndpoints as watching 'other endpoint types or labels' when the actual coupling is to topology labels.
clusters.rationale: Verified in topology.go: the added note reads 'If you modify the logic over here to  watch other endpoint types or labels' — the double space is present and the wording is loose. Typo-level.

clusters.summary: Adversarial subcases from the deleted Test_getNodeIPs / Test_waitForPodCIDR (a node whose only address is a malformed 'invalid-ip' string retried until fixed, the concurrent multi-goroutine fetch check, and a delete event during the wait) were not carried into the new tests, so that GetNodeHostIPs error path is no longer exercised anywhere.
clusters.rationale: The subcases named (invalid-ip retry, 3-goroutine concurrent fetch, delete-during-wait) genuinely were not ported into node_test.go, but the load-bearing conclusion is contradicted: TestNewNodeManager has two cases asserting `expectedError: "host IP unknown; known addresses: []"`, which is exactly the GetNodeHostIPs error path. What remains is a low-value coverage nit.

clusters.summary: The node-mutation test helpers discard the errors returned by fake-client Create/Update calls, so a silent test-setup failure surfaces later as a confusing unrelated assertion failure instead of a clear setup error.
clusters.rationale: True and trivial: node_test.go uses `_, _ = client.CoreV1().Nodes().Create(ctx, makeNode(), metav1.CreateOptions{})` in TestNewNodeManager's update closures and in TestNodeManagerOnNodeDelete/TestNodeManagerNode, while TestNodeManagerOnNodeChange does check with require.NoError. Test hygiene only.

clusters.summary: TestNodeManagerNode passes a node with no addresses into OnNodeChange, which hits the GetNodeHostIPs error early-return, so the test passes only incidentally and asserts nothing about that error path.
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: TestNodeManagerNode calls `nodeManager.OnNodeChange(makeNode(tweakResourceVersion("2")))` with no tweakNodeIPs, so GetNodeHostIPs fails and OnNodeChange logs and returns early; the assertion `require.Equal(t, "2", nodeManager.Node().ResourceVersion)` only passes because `n.node = node` ran before the validation. The test silently exercises the error path while claiming to test the happy path.

clusters.summary: TestNodeManagerNode passes time.Nanosecond poll interval and timeout, but the pre-populated node makes the very first immediate check succeed, so the polling/retry loop is never actually exercised and the nanosecond literals are misleading.
clusters.rationale: Accurate: TestNodeManagerNode calls newNodeManager(..., time.Nanosecond, time.Nanosecond) after creating the node and WaitForNamedCacheSync, and PollUntilContextCancel with immediate=true runs the condition once before any timeout check, so the loop never iterates. Misleading literals only — the test is deterministic.

clusters.summary: TestNodeManagerNode never mutates the *v1.Node returned by Node(), so a regression where Node() hands back the shared internal pointer instead of a deep copy would still pass the test.
clusters.rationale: True: TestNodeManagerNode only asserts nodeManager.Node().ResourceVersion == "1" then "2"; it never mutates the returned *v1.Node, so removing DeepCopy() would not fail it. A test-strength observation about intentional (known_safe) behavior, no defect in the production code.

clusters.summary: Every exit test injects a fake exitFunc that returns normally, unlike production os.Exit which never returns, so code after exitFunc(1) executes in tests but is dead in production — the tests exercise a path that cannot occur and cannot catch bugs in it.
clusters.rationale: Real fidelity gap: newNodeManager is given `func(i int) {}` / `exitFunc := func(code int) { exitCode = &code }`, which return, whereas production passes os.Exit. In OnNodeChange the PodCIDR-change branch calls n.exitFunc(1) and then falls through to the GetNodeHostIPs/NodeIP comparison, so tests execute a continuation that is unreachable in production and cannot distinguish which exit path fired.

clusters.summary: The ipvs proxier's OnTopologyChange does not set needFullSync=true while the iptables and nftables implementations of the same method do, an undocumented behavioral divergence discoverable only by reading all three backends.
clusters.rationale: The divergence is pre-existing and structural, not introduced here: the ipvs Proxier struct in the diff has no needFullSync field (its equivalent comment block is about initialSync), and the deleted ipvs OnNodeAdd/OnNodeUpdate/OnNodeDelete likewise never set needFullSync while the iptables/nftables ones did. OnTopologyChange preserves each backend's prior behavior.

clusters.summary: No proxier test references OnTopologyChange at all, so metaProxier's fan-out of the call to both the ipv4 and ipv6 sub-proxiers is untested and a dropped delegation would go unnoticed; the new by-reference map storage contract is likewise untested.
clusters.rationale: Consistent with the diff (no proxier test file is touched and the only OnTopologyChange consumer under test is config_test.go's mock), but the untested code is a three-line fan-out `proxier.ipv4Proxier.OnTopologyChange(...); proxier.ipv6Proxier.OnTopologyChange(...)`. The 'by-reference map' half is not a defect: handleNodeEvent builds a fresh map per event and never mutates it after publishing.

clusters.summary: With Test_getNodeIPs, Test_waitForPodCIDR and TestProxyServer_platformSetup deleted, nothing covers the server.Run() startup wiring (handlers registered against an already-synced informer under -race), leaving the startup race undetected.
clusters.rationale: The deletions are real (Test_getNodeIPs, Test_waitForPodCIDR, TestProxyServer_platformSetup all removed), but the causal premise is wrong: those tests exercised getNodeIPs/waitForPodCIDR/platformSetup, never server.Run()'s informer wiring, so no Run() coverage was lost. What is left is a generic 'Run() is untested' observation.

clusters.summary: The dual-stack (two PodCIDRs) case asserted by the deleted TestProxyServer_platformSetup was not carried forward — TestNewNodeManager supplies only a single CIDR — so dual-stack PodCIDR handling is no longer explicitly tested.
clusters.rationale: TestNewNodeManager's PodCIDR cases do use only `tweakPodCIDRs("10.0.0.0/24")`, but dual-stack PodCIDRs are still exercised elsewhere in the new tests (TestNodeManagerOnNodeChange uses initialPodCIDRs {"10.0.0.0/8","fd01:2345::/64"}), and PodCIDRs() is a plain `return n.node.Spec.PodCIDRs` passthrough — a low-value coverage nit.
